failure_modes.title: Under-rejected subject-position definitional sentences without exact-match seed
failure_modes.symptom: L missed links when the component mention appears in subject-position of a definitional sentence and the predicate gives role or relation information, but the sentence lacks a strong exact-match repetition beyond the initial mention. The missed cases use head-noun plus predicate patterns such as 'X is ...' or 'X connects to ...' rather than repeated namespace-prefix or list-style naming.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: The current bank is empty, so there is no extraction rule that promotes subject-position plus copular or relational predicate as sufficient evidence for a link. This allows under-rejected cases where only exact-match-heavy or enumeration-like forms are favored.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add extraction rules for subject-position component mentions followed by a copular predicate, apposition, or relational predicate. The rule should treat 'X is ...', 'X acts as ...', and 'X connects to ...' as positive when X is the antecedent of the sentence and the predicate describes structure, responsibility, or cross-reference to another component.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The Alpha unit is the entry point for back-end processing." -> link to the subject-position mention.
FP: "The entry point for back-end processing is described in the next section." -> no link because the head-noun phrase is generic and lacks a subject-position component antecedent.

failure_modes.title: Missed alias-of relation between abbreviated head-noun and multi-word-phrase mention
failure_modes.symptom: L missed links where a shortened form in subject-position is an alias-of a longer multi-word-phrase introduced nearby. The linker appears not to propagate from the abbreviated head-noun to the same component when the surrounding predicate describes responsibilities or connections.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: No alias-of rule exists to connect a shorter mention to a previously introduced multi-word-phrase or appositive expansion. Without this, abbreviated subject-position mentions are treated as ambiguous or generic and are under-linked.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add alias-of patterns for local abbreviation formation, apposition, and immediate antecedent reuse. If a multi-word-phrase is introduced and a later sentence uses its head-noun or shortened form in subject-position, propagate the same component unless a competing antecedent is closer.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The Delta Module handles coordination. Delta connects to the persistence layer." -> second sentence should inherit alias-of from the first.
FP: "The Delta Module handles coordination. The module connects to the persistence layer." -> do not force alias-of if multiple module antecedents are available in the local window.

failure_modes.title: Missed sub-element-of and container-of propagation from class-list sentence to following sentence
failure_modes.symptom: L missed links when one sentence introduces a container-of relation through a list of sub-elements, and the next sentence refers back to one listed item in subject-position. The second sentence should inherit the component link through antecedent propagation from the prior list context.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: There is no co-reference or propagated rule connecting a listed sub-element mention in one sentence to a following sentence where that same head-noun becomes the subject-position antecedent. As a result, local discourse continuity is ignored.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add co-reference rules for list-to-followup propagation: when a sentence enumerates sub-elements-of a component, and the next sentence starts with one listed item as subject-position, inherit the same component link unless contradicted by a nearer antecedent.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The Omega package contains Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. Alpha coordinates access to external storage." -> second sentence should link through sub-element-of/container-of propagation.
FP: "The Omega package contains Alpha, Beta, and Gamma. Access to external storage is coordinated carefully." -> no propagation because there is no subject-position antecedent matching a listed sub-element.

failure_modes.title: Over-approved links from generic definite-article head-noun phrases in predicate or modifier position
failure_modes.symptom: L over-approved links when a sentence contains a generic definite-article phrase or broad head-noun in predicate or modifier position, and the linker attached it to a component despite weak anchoring. These cases likely mention broad architectural function without a clear subject-position component antecedent.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: No validation rule rejects generic head-noun phrases that lack exact-match, alias-of support, or local antecedent support. This permits partial-match overreach from broad nouns and descriptive predicates.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add validation rules that down-rank or reject links triggered only by definite-article plus generic head-noun phrases in predicate, modifier, or object position unless supported by exact-match, apposition, namespace-prefix, or a strong antecedent chain.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The Zeta service stores audit records." -> link because the subject-position multi-word-phrase is explicit.
FP: "The storage of audit records is handled efficiently." -> no link because the definite-article head-noun phrase is generic and lacks a component antecedent.

failure_modes.title: Missed cross-reference from relational predicate to target component mention
failure_modes.symptom: L missed links where the sentence predicate explicitly states a relation to another component using a cross-reference phrase such as 'connects to', 'accesses', or 'acts as bridge to', but the target-side mention was not accepted as linked evidence.
failure_modes.apparent_cause: The current judge layer has no rule that treats relational predicates as bidirectional evidence for the mentioned target component. Without such a rule, only the subject-side mention may be considered, and the target-side mention is under-rejected.
failure_modes.suggested_direction: Add judge rules that recognize relational predicates and approve the target mention when it appears as the object of a clear cross-reference phrase. Constrain by exact-match or alias-of on the target mention to avoid broad propagation.
failure_modes.abstract_example_pair:
TP: "The Alpha unit connects to the Beta layer for persistence." -> approve both subject-side and target-side mentions.
FP: "The Alpha unit improves persistence behavior." -> do not infer a target component because no explicit cross-reference target is named.
